principles.title: Single canonical authority
principles.rule: Every behavior, state transition and shared capability must have one named canonical owner. Parallel authorities for the same responsibility are forbidden.

principles.title: Context before capability
principles.rule: Tenant, actor, environment and operating context must be resolved before capability, route, mutation or policy selection. Null or ambiguous context fails closed.

principles.title: Truth has an explicit owner
principles.rule: Commerce truth, identity truth, release truth and compatibility truth are server-owned or authority-owned. Presentation layers may display truth but may not invent or override it.

principles.title: Development and release are separate transactions
principles.rule: A coherent Development Transaction may span multiple subsystems, but production changes are assembled and proven as explicit Release Transactions with closed dependency scope.

principles.title: Dependency closure before release
principles.rule: A Release Transaction must include every runtime, policy, schema, knowledge and regression dependency required for the selected change-set. Missing closure blocks release.

principles.title: Fail closed on authority failure
principles.rule: Authentication, authorization, payment, schema compatibility, release provenance and critical configuration failures must default to denial or safe non-action.

principles.title: Adapters isolate external providers
principles.rule: External providers are connected through stable platform contracts. Core business logic may not depend directly on provider-specific transport or payload semantics.

principles.title: State transitions are explicit
principles.rule: Source, persisted state, runtime materialization and production state are distinct authorities. Every required transition between them must be named and provable.

principles.title: Evidence does not become truth by implication
principles.rule: CI green, preview readiness, screenshots, fixtures and historical documents are evidence only. They do not replace runtime, schema, identity or production authority.

principles.title: Known failures become prevention
principles.rule: Every recurring or material defect must be converted into durable knowledge, regression authority, policy, or deterministic detection so the same failure class moves earlier in the lifecycle.

principles.title: Clean replacement
principles.rule: When an authority is superseded, obsolete implementations, routes, tests and documentation must be removed or explicitly time-bounded as compatibility layers.

principles.title: Machine identity is stable
principles.rule: Machine-consumed authorities, domains, failures and contracts require stable identifiers independent of mutable display names or human labels.

principles.title: Architecture is queryable
principles.rule: The system architecture must be represented in machine-readable form so ownership, dependencies, surfaces and impact can be resolved deterministically.

principles.title: Autonomy remains governed
principles.rule: Automation and future AI may diagnose, propose and execute only within explicit policy, authority and evidence boundaries. Direct code or production mutation is never inferred from model confidence alone.

supersession.rule: Existing architecture documents remain supporting evidence unless explicitly registered as canonical domain authority.
